text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose or average blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your blood glucose or average blood sugar levels

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors use the following threshold values according to guidelines from the American Diabetes Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. No fasting is required.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after going without food or drink (except water) for at least 8 hours.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar before and two hours after you drink a sweet liquid containing 75 grams of glucose.
Diabetes: 200 mg/dL or higher at the two-hour mark
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time of day when you have classic symptoms of high blood sugar.
Repeat Testing: Unless you have clear, severe symptoms and a random reading over 200 mg/dL, doctors usually confirm a diabetes diagnosis with a repeat test on a second separate day.
Common Symptoms: Many people have no early symptoms, but signs can include extreme thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss, and fatigue.
